headline: Enveda reports Claude-based review of four clinical GMP batch records
summary: Enveda’s Oct 27 report describes CDP, a Claude-based advisory system for reviewing executed pharmaceutical manufacturing records. On four records comprising 1,061 scanned pages from one Phase 2 campaign, Enveda reports that CDP raised all 11 distinct actionable issues found by human reviewers in at least one run, and a Claude Opus 4.7 pass added seven adjudicator-confirmed actionable comments. CDP processing plus a human quality check took 166 minutes versus 1,553 minutes for unaided internal manual review, a reported 9.4-fold time reduction. The study is exploratory and company-reported; reviewers had access to some earlier-step records unavailable to CDP, each run contained one misread, about 79% of CDP comments needed no action, and the system remains advisory rather than validated as a GMP computerized system. These results do not establish general reliability, total-cost savings, regulatory approval or improved drug quality.
